method_lane.reason: The brief refers to one method paragraph but does not identify a single hypothesis as the assigned lane. H1 is a ranked proposal, not an authorization.

ranking_basis: Qualitative prior ranking of potential improvement in a spatially blocked HOLDOUT-DTI evaluation, balanced against cost. These ranks are not scores, deltas, calibrated forecasts, or evidence of performance.
novelty_scope: Not implemented or tested in this repository's present review lane. The currently observed refs for all nine priority sites have changed since the pinned rasters; their new contents have not been audited. Therefore no claim is made that these ideas have never been tried anywhere across the fleet.

hypotheses.title: Depth-shifted, multiscale gravity–magnetic discontinuity
hypotheses.potential_label: Highest qualitative potential of this shortlist; untested
layers: depth_to_base_surf (owner-mirror band 15; official metadata says conductive-base depth, not verified basement depth)
hypotheses.signature: At several fixed spatial scales, compare signed gravity-edge normals with magnetic-gradient ridges at a bounded cross-normal offset informed by a depth/dip proxy; test both magnetic polarities and retain only scale-persistent paired edges.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A buried structural discontinuity may juxtapose density and magnetic properties beneath basin fill where a surface trace is weak or absent. The proposal uses subsurface physical-property contrasts rather than catalogue proximity. This is a plausible target for unmapped segments, not proof that the catalogue omits only surface-visible faults.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: Different as proposed from the named pseudo-gravity residual, simple potential-field fusion, dotted-ridge, catalogue-gap and geothermal-PINN families: it tests a depth-conditioned spatial offset between paired signed edge responses. Related methods elsewhere are not exhaustively audited.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: An unfaulted lithologic contact or intrusive dike can produce aligned gravity and magnetic edges; flight-line striping and gridding artefacts can also create apparent paired boundaries.
hypotheses.data_status: The 19-band feature names are recorded in a hash-checked owner mirror, not an authenticated DrivenData download. The raw owner-mirrored stack and 19 raw bands were reverified in this session’s ignored cache; they may not persist, are not organizer-authenticated, and the shared derived feature bank is absent. Verify provenance before any run.

hypotheses.title: Conductive-flank asymmetry conditioned on a potential-field edge
hypotheses.potential_label: Moderate qualitative potential; overlaps a previously explored family
layers: depth_to_base_surf (owner-mirror band 15; official metadata terminology must be retained)
hypotheses.signature: Estimate signed conductivity contrast on opposite sides of a persistent gravity edge, normalize each flank against its local background and depth, and test whether the asymmetry is stable across scales rather than using raw conductivity or a symmetric buffer.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A concealed fault-related fluid or alteration pathway could make the two flanks electrically asymmetric even where a mapped trace is missing. It is a conditional physical-property test, not a rule that high conductivity means a fault.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: The proposed statistic is a signed, edge-conditioned cross-flank contrast rather than simple co-location or a vent-proximity prior. However, the user-provided history includes conductivity/flank-labelled methods, so this is not claimed to be globally novel and should rank below H1 unless exact old code shows a meaningful distinction.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Saline basin fill, clay-rich strata, groundwater, and non-faulted lithologic boundaries can all create conductivity asymmetry.
hypotheses.data_status: Uses bands named in the owner-mirrored numerical feature stack; the restored raw owner-mirror bands are not authenticated as original competition bytes, and the shared derived feature bank is absent.

hypotheses.title: Repeated cross-drainage deflection across a candidate structure
hypotheses.potential_label: Lower qualitative potential; external-data feasibility unverified
layers: USGS 3DEP bare-earth digital elevation model (specific tiles and resolution not established here)
hypotheses.signature: Derive channels from absolute elevation, measure repeated channel azimuth changes, knickzones, and opposing-bank relief across the same candidate line, and normalize by upstream contributing area; require several independent crossings rather than a single scarp.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A buried or eroded fault may deflect multiple channels without leaving a continuous scarp, creating a geomorphic expression beyond catalogue segment endpoints. Channel behaviour is supporting evidence, not a fault label.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: Different from single-scarp, slope-asymmetry, chi-corridor and dotted-ridge methods because it tests repeated cross-channel geometry using an absolute DEM and catchment normalization. Fleet-wide novelty is unverified.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts, differential erosion, alluvial fans, inherited drainage, capture, roads, and terraces can deflect channels.
hypotheses.data_status: Not viable in this checkout until the exact official DEM tiles, coverage, resolution and permitted download are verified; none were downloaded.

external_data.access_check: The cited USGS page is recorded in the source register as describing free, unrestricted 3DEP products. Study-area tile coverage and actual binary access have not been checked; therefore the data are not yet verified obtainable for this experiment.

hypotheses.title: Cross-flight-line repeatability of buried magnetic edges
hypotheses.potential_label: Lowest direct prediction potential; primarily an artefact-control experiment
layers: USGS GeoDAWN magnetic flight-line observations and acquisition-direction metadata
mag_anom (owner-mirror band 1) and tmi_hg (owner-mirror band 3) for gridded comparison
hypotheses.signature: Estimate edge normals independently from crossing flight-line directions and retain only anomalies whose location and orientation are reproducible across acquisition directions; use disagreement as an artefact veto, not as a positive fault label.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A real subsurface physical-property boundary potentially associated with an unmapped fault should be spatially stable across independent acquisition directions, unlike some flight-line artefacts. This test improves measurement reliability; it does not establish that a stable edge is a fault.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: This is an acquisition-geometry robustness test, not another point-density, terrain-scarp, geothermal-proximity, or catalogue-gap score. No local implementation is present; fleet-wide novelty is unverified.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: A lithologic contact, dike, or non-fault magnetic body is also stable across flight directions; uneven line coverage can create false disagreement.
hypotheses.data_status: The USGS release page is recorded as listing flight-line data and grids, but the line-level files and usable crossing coverage were not downloaded or verified in this environment. Not viable here until that check succeeds.
